proelĭāris (prael- ) and proelĭā-lis , e, adj. proelium,
I.of or belonging to a battle (ante- and post-class.): “pugnae proeliares,” pitched battles, Plaut. Curc. 4, 4, 17 : “acies,” App. M. 8, p. 208, 40 : proeliares dies appellantur, quibus fas est hostem bello lacessere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 266 Müll.; “called also proeliales dies,” Macr. 1, 16 : “proeliaris dea,” i. e. Minerva, App. M. 10, p. 254, 21 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
